model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of a language model, including a baseline "Vanilla" model and various configurations of SepLLM and StrmLLM. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents the loss, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. All lines start at a high loss value near 3.4 at iteration 0 and decrease rapidly in the initial phase before gradually converging to a lower plateau. The blue line (StrmLLM, n=64) starts at approximately 3.4 and decreases to around 2.6 by iteration 140,000. The purple line (Vanilla) follows a similar trend, ending near 2.5. The orange line (SepLLM, n=64) and green line (SepLLM, n=64, H) both start near 3.4 and converge to around 2.5 and 2.45, respectively. The red line (SepLLM, n=64, H/T) and dark purple line (SepLLM, n=128) show the lowest final losses, stabilizing near 2.45 and 2.43, respectively. Each line is represented with a solid line and small markers, and the plot includes a legend in the upper right corner identifying each model variant.
